messages.subject: Stood down as directed - measurement was already complete; classification rule below
messages.body: Acknowledged the stand-down; I had already finished the full measurement (hash-verified against the real 204 documents, not the dataset-as-population) by the time it arrived, so nothing was left mid-flight and the corpus was never touched. CLASSIFICATION TEST, in full, for distinguishing a genuine section from a contents/table/footnote row -- reusable directly for the endnote fix: for every SECTION_RE match in a document, compute the character gap to the match before and after it; a table of provisions, an endnote/amendment block, or an in-Act cross-reference schedule is a SUSTAINED RUN of 5 or more consecutive matches each connected by a gap under 300 characters (this corpus's own evidence: a 125-row endnote block has median gap ~144 chars, 28 real Part IIIC sections have median gap ~1,406), so a run of that shape and length is a table and none of its rows are provisions; anything not in such a run is presumptively genuine. This automated rule is not perfect at the edges -- a short real section sitting right next to where an unrelated table starts (commonly an Act's own trailing 'Notes' block) can get swept in by proximity alone -- so I read every one of the 29 headings it flagged as junk in this corpus (small enough to check in full) and hand-corrected 6 true positives, each with the real quoted excerpt as the reason, while only spot-checking a sample of the 163 it called genuine rather than reviewing all of them exhaustively. Final, manually-verified figures I'd already reached: 192 headings recovered across the 204 legacy documents (upper bound), 169 of them genuine operative sections (actual damage), 23 table/contents junk, zero regressions, Privacy Act (document 480) reproduced separately at +4 genuine/0 junk/0 lost as required. Everything -- the two working scripts, the per-document and per-heading JSONL breakdowns, the dataset-match log, and the full write-up with worked examples for each class -- is at C:\Users\Alpha\AppData\Local\Temp\parser_damage\ (PARSER_DAMAGE_REPORT.md is the entry point); repo root is clean, and the only working-tree change present (src/michael/ingest.py, a logging-path edit) is WORKER-4's concurrent work, not mine -- I confirmed it doesn't touch any parser logic I measured against and left it untouched.

messages.subject: Recalibration prep ready, not run
messages.body: Added 6 Privacy Act Part IIIC queries (incl. required s26WD) to calibration/labelled_queries.json, verified against real corpus text read over Railway ssh; re-checked all 10 known-absent entries by reading the current document list and confirmed none are newly covered, so none retired. Spend estimate for one calibration run is ~600 tokens of query-only embedding, about $0.000012 at OpenAI's list rate -- the corpus never needs re-embedding. Left the run un-executed as instructed; pytest is green (153 passed) and mypy is clean on my files, with 7 pre-existing errors in an untracked backups/compare.py outside my scope; full per-entry verdicts, the diff, and void-conditions are in my report above.

messages.subject: Fixed: every ingestion path now writes the file log; README corrected
messages.body: Added a single log_attempt() call inside _write() (the shared insert point for ingest_url, ingest_file and seed_from_corpus) so every successful ingestion writes the file log, and wrapped ingest_file's own check_url() so its host refusal is logged too -- both gaps confirmed closed by three new tests in tests/test_ingest.py (file ingest, URL ingest via a mocked fetch, and a refusal), all against a fake DB connection so no socket opens, and I rewrote README.md's 'Purging documents...' paragraph to lead with the 205-rows-vs-3-lines finding and state the file log now covers every path, plus added the owner's requested not-self-rebuilding note (documents holds no text, provisions.char_start/char_end point into text kept nowhere) right beside it. uv run pytest is green (153 passed, 5 deselected) and uv run mypy . is clean on every file I touched -- the only remaining mypy errors are 7 pre-existing ones in the untracked backups/compare.py, which is the owner's own CSV-comparison script, outside WORKER-4's scope, and something I did not create or edit. Nothing left on this task except your review; I did not touch the 205-row backfill question (recommended in my report, not acted on), calibration/labelled_queries.json, or backups/ -- full diffs, call-site table, and test output are in the attached report.
